art.title: Martin Luther
art.why: The very subject. FLAG: the NGA record has no description (assistivetext empty), so Stage B cannot write look points from it; if none can be written, use null for this session's look.

art.title: Portrait of a Man
art.why: No printing press or church door in the NGA. Cranach was Luther's friend in Wittenberg and his workshop printed Luther's books (the September Testament, 1522): the face of the world the theses reached, painted the year the printed German New Testament appeared. Say plainly the sitter is unknown.

art.title: Woman and Child in a Courtyard
art.why: Ordinary home life in a Protestant Dutch town: the everyday vocation Luther's 'servant of all' made holy.

art.title: Memory Copy of Holbein's Erasmus
art.why: Erasmus, after Holbein's portrait. FLAG: no NGA description and no date; Stage B can only describe it if a description is available, otherwise null.

art.title: Cardinal Pietro Bembo
art.why: No council or Ignatius in the NGA. Bembo was made cardinal by Paul III, the pope who called the Council of Trent and approved the Jesuits (1540): a churchman of the Catholic reform, painted the year the Jesuits were founded.

art.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Catherine
art.why: No More or Tudor martyrdom in the NGA. A martyrdom painted in the Low Countries in the decade the persecutions began there; the lecture must say this is an early-church saint, not a Reformation martyr.

art.title: In Church
art.why: Ordinary people side by side in a pew: worship that both traditions still share, for the verdict.
